title: HAPPY YOUNG WOMEN, GRUMPY OLD MEN? EMOTION-DRIVEN DEMOGRAPHIC BIASES IN SYNTHETIC FACE GENERATION

bias_targets.methodology: Generating synthetic faces using text-to-image models with various emotion prompts, classifying the gender of the outputs using the FairFace model, and comparing the resulting distributions against global population statistics and neutral baselines using Kullback-Leibler (KL) and Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergences.

Generating synthetic faces using text-to-image models with different emotion prompts, classifying the race of the generated faces using the FairFace model, and comparing the racial distributions to global population estimates and neutral baselines using information-theoretic divergence metrics.

Generating synthetic faces using text-to-image models, estimating the age groups of the generated faces using the FairFace classifier, and comparing the output age distributions against global population statistics and neutral baselines to quantify ageism and under-representation.

Estimating the facial attractiveness (low, medium, high) of the generated images using a specialized ResNet-based classifier and evaluating how different emotional prompts shift the distribution of attractiveness scores to study the attractiveness halo effect.
